baseline.description: The global-register and composite-object lowering fixes are present; the pointer-specific ruling is not implemented.

declaredCapabilities: A pointer-to-integer or non-null integer-to-pointer conversion reports E3036 at the conversion; a null pointer constant still lowers.
An uninitialized object or function pointer is a typed EvoIR poison value with absent provenance.
Pointer poison may cross CFG edges without being consumed and may be overwritten before use.
Dereferencing pointer poison reports E3013 in both interpreters.
The validator and Section 9 reader accept and round-trip uninitialized.ptr and uninitialized.fnptr.

declaredFailures.observed: Both conversion directions report E3101; pointer-to-integer retains the free-text diagnostic integer expression has a non-bit-vector EvoIR value.
Lowering reports E3101 non-integer scalar type is outside Day 6 while constructing an absent incoming pointer value.
The C-HIR interpreter reports E3001 read-of-uninitialized-object before the EvoIR half is reached.

protectedExistingBehavior.result: PASS: the generic Inst::Uninitialized representation already validates and round-trips ptr<generic> and fnptr signatures exactly.
The same test pins that (int *)0 remains accepted.

workspaceRun.result: Every pre-existing test target passed; lowering_diagnostic_frontier had exactly the three declared failures and five passes; uninitialized_pointer passed.

rejectedEvidence: The first base-layout invocation could not access the sealed container inside the restricted sandbox and exited 1 without output; it is not evidence. The permission-correct rerun above is the recorded result.
claimCeiling: This checkpoint proves three declared semantic RED failures and one protected generic IR/text capability. It makes no implementation or survey claim.
